statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-58042 is a denial of service in Node.js: the parsers for A, AAAA and ANY DNS replies used fixed 256-entry stack arrays for address and TTL records, so a reply to dns.resolveAny() with more than 256 A records aborted the process. Node.js fixed it for 24.x in 24.18.1, released 2026-07-29: the July 2026 security release, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/july-2026-security-releases, lists 24.x among the affected release lines, and the 24.18.1 release notes, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.18.1, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/9d0d36cffd ('dns: handle large resolveAny address replies'), which carries CVE-ID: CVE-2026-58042 and is in the v24.18.1 tag and not in v24.18.0; outside tests it changes src/cares_wrap.cc. The CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-58042, lists Node.js 24 releases up to 24.18.0 as affected. The DHI nodejs-24 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from the upstream Node.js release tarball for their version. Each published nodejs-24 package holds one file, /usr/bin/node, a dynamically linked musl program that carries the Node.js JavaScript library and the C++ runtime where this code lives; the nodejs-24-dev subpackages hold C and C++ header files and two .gypi build configuration files under /usr/include/node, and the nodejs-24-doc subpackages hold the node man page and two debugger helper files, gdbinit and lldb_commands.py, with no ELF, PE or Mach-O file in either. We checked the node binary, /usr/bin/node, in every nodejs-24 package for Alpine 3.23 published by 2026-11-27, on x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 24.18.1-r0, 24.19.0-r0, 24.20.0-r0, 24.21.0-r0, 24.22.0-r0, 24.22.1-r0, 24.22.1-r1, 24.22.2-r0 and 24.22.3-r0 report v24.18.1 through v24.22.3 and carry the fix, while the earlier builds 24.13.0-r0, 24.13.1-r0, 24.14.0-r0, 24.14.1-r0, 24.15.0-r0, 24.15.0-r1, 24.16.0-r0, 24.17.0-r0 and 24.18.0-r0 report v24.13.0 through v24.18.0 and are affected. As a check, this fix is C++ code with no new string, so we read the machine code of the exported reply parsers in the node binary. The fix replaces the 256-entry stack arrays with heap buffers sized from the reply's answer count. On x86_64 the A, AAAA and ANY parsers (node::cares_wrap::ATraits, AaaaTraits and AnyTraits::Parse) reserve stack frames of 0x8f8, 0x14f8 and 0x1d88 bytes in 24.18.0-r0 and every earlier build, and 0xf8, 0x108 and 0x1a8 bytes in 24.18.1-r0 and every later build; on aarch64 the A parser's frame drops from 0x8b0 to 0x120 bytes at 24.18.1-r0, and all three parsers have fixed frames of 0x120, 0x110 and 0x1e0 bytes from then on. In 24.18.1-r0 on both architectures the three parsers call operator new, eight calls in all, and in 24.16.0-r0, 24.17.0-r0 and 24.18.0-r0 they call it none. 24.18.1-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
